brand-violet.$description: Brand Violet — Violet supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

tinted-highlight.$description: Tinted Highlight — Light supporting surface for subtle backgrounds and section separation.

ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Headline text, primary copy at full weight — the deepest near-black, used wherever the system needs maximum contrast on white

graphite.$description: Graphite — Secondary text, button labels on filled surfaces, dark UI chrome where pure black is too heavy

slate.$description: Slate — Body text, paragraph copy, subheadings — the working gray for sustained reading

mid-gray.$description: Mid Gray — Icon strokes, list markers, muted labels, secondary metadata — high-frequency utilitarian gray

steel.$description: Steel — Input placeholders, helper text, disabled states

mist.$description: Mist — Input borders at rest, slightly stronger divider lines, de-emphasized outlines

fog.$description: Fog — Default hairline borders, card outlines, table dividers, subtle structural separation

cloud.$description: Cloud — Page canvas, section background behind cards — the off-white that lifts content without being clinical

paper.$description: Paper — Card surfaces, nav bar, button text on violet, input fields — the bright top layer

satoshi.$description: Single-family geometric sans used for everything from 14px helper text up to 60px display headlines. Satoshi's rounded geometric forms give the violet-and-white system a friendlier edge than a neutral grotesque — the open apertures and soft terminals keep even the 700-weight display lines from feeling corporate. Weight 700 owns the hero and section headlines; 600 handles subheadings and emphasized body; 500 is reserved for button labels and badge text; 400 carries paragraphs and UI labels. Free substitute: 'Inter' or 'General Sans' (Fontshare) as the closest open-license match.
